chief_complaint: Respiratory concerns related to non‑small cell lung cancer and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (emphysema)
history_of_present_illness: The patient is a 66‑year‑old man with a history of stage 1 non‑small cell lung cancer diagnosed in April 2005, managed with surgery and adjuvant chemotherapy (paclitaxel, cisplatin). He also has pulmonary emphysema diagnosed in 2003, requiring daily inhaled corticosteroid/long‑acting beta‑agonist therapy and rescue albuterol. Over the past years he has accumulated 20 inpatient admissions, multiple thoracic CT scans (notably ten on a single day in April 2007), and a small number of outpatient visits, reflecting intensive oncologic and pulmonary care. Co‑morbid hypertension (treated with a three‑drug regimen), obesity, pre‑diabetes, chronic anemia, and hip osteoarthritis are also present and contribute to overall clinical complexity. Social barriers such as longstanding transportation problems and a criminal record have limited outpatient follow‑up. The most recent documented encounter was in May 2007.

active_problems.name: Non‑small cell carcinoma of lung, stage 1 (TNM)

past_medical_history: Resolved conditions include acute viral pharyngitis, primary dental caries, social isolation, ankle sprain, colon polyp, and prior part‑time employment. An earlier episode of stress resolved in 2005. These historical issues are now inactive and do not currently influence care.

social_determinants: Patient reports longstanding transport problems and lack of reliable transportation, which have limited outpatient care access. He has a criminal record and is currently employed full‑time. He has attained higher education. These factors may affect adherence and follow‑up.
risk_factor_summary: Charlson comorbidity index is 1 (reflecting lung cancer). Clinical complexity is high with moderate polypharmacy (6 meds). Glycemic control is pre‑diabetic (A1c 5.8%). Blood pressure, heart rate, BMI, eGFR, and lipid panel are missing, preventing full cardiovascular risk assessment. Organ systems at elevated risk: respiratory (lung cancer, emphysema), cardiovascular (hypertension, obesity), metabolic (prediabetes), hematologic (anemia), musculoskeletal (osteoarthritis). Medications corroborate these risks.
